title: Mixed-language voices
intro_html:
Must the text be in the voice's language? For a Gemini voice, no. The voices are multilingual: the same voice speaks any supported language, and a line may switch language midway. Cloud TTS still requires a languageCode, which sets the output language and accent. It is the language the presenter is "from", which the other-locale configuration tests. The Gemini API's own TTS takes no language code at all and "detects the input language automatically". For a WaveNet voice, yes: each voice belongs to one locale (its name says which), and other languages are read with that language's phonetics unless SSML says otherwise.

Coverage. On Cloud TTS, Gemini-TTS lists about 25 GA languages, including Spanish, Russian, French, German, Italian and US English, and 75 or more in preview, including Mandarin and British English. The Gemini API's 3.8 Flash TTS claims more than 130 languages, and its Lite model more than 100. Quality falls off for rarer languages, which the docs do not quantify; "best effort" is the most any page promises.

Marking which part is in which language. The only standard is SSML <lang xml:lang="es-ES">. Cloud TTS supports it "on a best effort basis. Not all language combinations produce the same quality", all in one voice unless <voice> switches the speaker. Semitic languages are read as silence, and Japanese Kanji as Chinese. Gemini voices take plain text and a prompt, with no SSML and no per-span language field. The only tool is to say it in the prompt, and nothing in the API is unified across providers. Aura-1 is English only and ignores language entirely.

Sources: Cloud TTS: Gemini-TTS · Cloud TTS: SSML (<lang>, <voice>) · Gemini API: speech generation · Cloudflare: Aura-1

cards.title: Gemini 3.1, the prompt names each part's language
cards.why: Production's directed voice (Kore), with `languageCode` set to the presenter's language and a prompt saying which words are in which language. The only way to label a span for a Gemini voice is to say it in words.
cards.notes: Rate the configuration overall, after listening to the lines.

cards.title: The same, a second Gemini voice
cards.why: As above, in Charon (the guide voice here), to hear whether it is the model or the voice.
cards.notes: Rate the configuration overall, after listening to the lines.

cards.title: Gemini 3.1, no prompt
cards.why: The same voice with no prompt at all: only `languageCode` says what the line is. What the model does with a foreign phrase on its own.
cards.notes: Rate the configuration overall, after listening to the lines.

cards.title: Gemini 3.1, the quoted language's languageCode
cards.why: No prompt, and `languageCode` set to the *quoted* language instead of the presenter's. If the code sets the accent, the presenter's own words should now sound foreign.
cards.notes: Rate the configuration overall, after listening to the lines.

cards.title: Gemini 2.5 Flash TTS, no prompt
cards.why: Production's second directed model, no prompt: the older model's handling of the switch.
cards.notes: Rate the configuration overall, after listening to the lines.

cards.title: Gemini API 3.8 Flash TTS, language detected
cards.why: The Gemini API's newest voice on the free key: no language code exists in the request, so the model decides everything. Not a production path today.
cards.notes: Rate the configuration overall, after listening to the lines.

cards.title: WaveNet, the presenter's voice
cards.why: Production's clear voice for the presenter's language, plain text. A WaveNet voice speaks one language, so the quoted words are read with its phonetics.
cards.notes: Rate the configuration overall, after listening to the lines.

cards.title: WaveNet with SSML <lang>
cards.why: The same voice, each quoted span wrapped in `<lang xml:lang=…>`, SSML's standard way of labelling a span's language. Cloud TTS supports it “on a best effort basis”.
cards.notes: Rate the configuration overall, after listening to the lines.

cards.title: WaveNet with SSML <voice>: a second speaker
cards.why: Each quoted span handed to that language's own WaveNet voice with `<voice name=…>`, in one request: two people, each in their own language.
cards.notes: Rate the configuration overall, after listening to the lines.

cards.title: Cloudflare Aura-1 (English lines only)
cards.why: Deepgram's Aura-1 on Cloudflare: English only, no language field, no direction. Only the English-led lines are sent.
cards.notes: Rate the configuration overall, after listening to the lines.
